title: Spicy Crispy Chicken Burger
changes_from_base: Same buttermilk-brined, double-coated fried thighs as the Classic Chicken Burger, with hot sauce added to the buttermilk. After frying, the chicken is brushed with a cayenne hot-oil glaze and served with a cool, crunchy slaw and pickles instead of plain lettuce and mayo.
summary: Buttermilk-marinated fried chicken with a craggy, extra-crisp coating, brushed with a smoky-sweet hot glaze and piled onto a cool, crunchy slaw.
equipment: large heavy pot or deep casserole (at least 24 cm wide)
wire rack set over a tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
hot pepper sauce (vinegar-based, such as a Louisiana-style sauce)
neutral oil, for the hot glaze
soft burger buns or brioche-style buns
white or red cabbage, finely shredded
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.text: Submerge the chicken thighs in buttermilk mixed with salt, garlic powder, paprika and 2 tablespoons of hot sauce, then cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to 24 hours. The buttermilk's acidity gently tenderises the meat while seasoning it right through.

steps.title: Build the dredge
steps.text: Combine flour, cornflour, baking powder, salt and pepper in a wide bowl, then rub in 2 tablespoons of the buttermilk marinade to form craggy little clumps. Cornflour and baking powder lighten the coating, while those damp clumps are what give the finished crust its extra-crunchy texture.

steps.title: Coat and rest the chicken
steps.text: Lift each piece from the buttermilk, letting the excess drip off, then press firmly into the dredge. Rest the coated pieces on a rack for 10 minutes so the coating hydrates; skipping this is the main reason coatings fall off in the oil.

steps.title: Fry the chicken
steps.text: Heat 5cm of oil in a heavy pot to 175°C and fry the chicken two pieces at a time for 6-8 minutes, turning once, keeping the oil between 150-165°C throughout. It's ready when deep golden and 74°C in the thickest part; drain on a rack rather than paper so the crust stays crisp instead of steaming.

steps.title: Make the hot glaze
steps.text: Warm the oil gently for about 1 minute in a small pan, just until it shimmers but is nowhere near smoking (about 120°C), then take it off the heat and whisk in cayenne, smoked paprika, brown sugar and garlic powder. Whisking off the heat stops the spices scorching and turning bitter.

steps.title: Glaze the chicken
steps.text: Brush the warm glaze generously over the hot fried chicken while it's still on the rack, stirring the glaze each time you dip in as the spices settle quickly. The heat from the chicken helps the glaze cling in a thin, sticky layer.

steps.title: Make the slaw
steps.text: Toss cabbage and carrot with mayo, Greek yoghurt, lemon juice and a pinch of salt just before serving. Mixing it at the last minute keeps the cabbage crisp rather than letting it wilt and turn watery.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Toast the buttered bun halves, cut side down, in a frying pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden, which gives the spicy sauce a crisp surface to sit on instead of soaking straight in.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Pile the slaw onto the bottom bun, top with the glazed chicken and a few pickles, then finish with the top bun. The cool, crunchy slaw underneath balances the heat and stickiness of the chicken above it.

tips: Rest the coated chicken on a rack for 10 minutes before frying - skipping this is the most common cause of the crust falling off in the oil.
Keep the oil between 160-170°C throughout frying; if it drops too low the coating turns greasy instead of crisp.
Stir the glaze each time you brush it on, since the spices settle quickly at the bottom of the pan.
Mix the slaw just before serving so the cabbage stays crunchy rather than wilting.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Fried chicken keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days; freezing isn't recommended as the coating turns soggy on thawing. Reheat in an oven until piping hot and 74°C at the centre - the microwave will soften the crust. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
